title: Experiment: a delegated task reaches a closed-stdin child and a tool call returns the exact challenge

facts.inference: local deterministic OpenAI-compatible fake provider on 127.0.0.1; no paid provider contacted

summary: TASK BINDING: a `--mode json -p <task> --no-session` child spawned with stdio stdin set to ignore — stdin genuinely closed — completed a turn with exit 0, and the exact task sentinel KILN-TASK-SENTINEL-9F3A was observed in the user message the provider received. The observation is taken at the provider boundary, not from anything the model said. CANARY SHAPE: when the provider returned a tool call, the registered custom tool executed and received `{"challenge":"abc123xyz"}` — the exact value — through the real pinned runtime. CONTROL A: a provider returning prose instead produced no tool execution. CONTROL B: the same request with the tool excluded from `--tools` produced no execution and the tool was not offered to the model. Both platforms agree on every row.
notes: ⚠️ TWO CONTROLS, BECAUSE ONE WOULD NOT DO. Without the prose control, 'the tool executed' could be an artefact of the fixture always executing it; without the exclusion control, the allowlist could be decorative. ⚠️ THE TOOL SIGNATURE IS execute(toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate, ctx) — the parameters are the SECOND argument. Reading the first argument as the parameters silently yields the tool-call id, which is how this run first reported a null challenge against a tool that had in fact been called correctly.
